caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 657 of 2010
lawyer:
Nahid Mahtab, Advocate instructed by Mrs Mahmuda Begum. Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Mr Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Anti-Corruption Commission  ------ Petitioner
Vs. 
AKM Shamim Hasan and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. This Criminal Petition for Leave to appeal has been filed by the petitioner against the Order dated 18-7-2010 passed a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 20319 of 2010. 

 3. Short facts necessary for disposal of this Leave Petition are that on a First Information Report (FIR) lodged by an Assistant Director, Dumiti Daman Commission, District Co-ordinate Office, Barisal, Kotwali Police Station Case No. 1 dated 5- 9-2008 under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, was started against the accused-respondent No.1 (hereinafter referred to as the accused). After investigation, the Dumiti Daman Commission submitted charge-sheet in the case against the accused on 12-1-2009 under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. Eventually, the case was transferred to the Court of Divisional Special Judge, Barisal for disposal and was registered as Special Case No.7 of 2009. It appears that the trial of the case had already commenced and after examination of as many as 23 prosecution witnesses, the petitioner was examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code) and he, after claiming himself to be innocent, wanted to examine defence witnesses and accordingly, on 14-06-2010 was fixed for examination of the defence witnesses. On this date, on the prayer of the accused, the next date was fixed on 30-6-2010 for examination of the defence witnesses. At that stage, the accused filed an application before the High Court Division under section 526 of the Code for transfer of the case from the Divisional Special Judge, Barisal to any other Judge of Dhaka Division or any other jurisdiction. The grounds, on which transfer of the case was sought, were that the Public Prosecutor who had been prosecuting the case on behalf of the Durniti Daman Commission, rebuked the accused in open Court in filthy language on several occasions which fact though was brought to the notice of the Divisional Special Judge, he did not pay any heed to the same which proved the biasness of the Divisional Special Judge and created an apprehension in the mind of he accused that he would not get fair and impartial justice from him. After examination of PW 1 on 9-6-1999 while prayer for adjournment was made for cross-examining him on the following day, the Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the prayer submitting that “এই স্বাক্ষীকে অদ্য জেরা করা না হলে, তাকে ফিরিয়ে ওেয়া হলে সে (পি,ডবলিউ-১ খুন হবে)” and this submission of the Public Prosecutor was also noted in the deposition sheet of PW 1 by the Divisional Special Judge and the above fact also strengthened the belief of the accused that he "will lose(sic) the case due to cause of one-eyed policy towards the prosecution by the present trial Court." 

 4. A Division Bench of the High Court Division which heard the said application allowed the same summarily and transferred the case from the Divisional Special Judge to the Sessions Judge, Barisal. 

 6. It is an admitted fact that after examination of 23 prosecution witnesses, the case was fixed for examination of the defence witnesses. From the statements made in the application under section 526 of the Code, it appears that the remark/comment made by the Public Prosecutor as quoted hereinbefore and as allegedly noted down in the deposition sheet of PW 1 by the Divisional Special Judge, was made on 9-6-2009 and thereafter 29 other witnesses were examined by the prosecution but the accused never felt that he would not get fair justice from the Divisional Special Judge and only after closure of the examination of the prosecution witnesses, he felt that he would not get fair justice from him. The function of the Public Prosecution is to produce witnesses on behalf of the prosecution and to examine them in accordance with law and to get the relevant documents proved by the witnesses in support of the prosecution case and to place the argument before the Court with reference to the evidence on record and the law. He cannot have and must not have any role to dispense justice by a Court and therefore, even if the case of the accused is accepted that the Public Prosecutor rebuked him and made comment while PW 1 was examined as quoted hereinbefore cannot be the grounds for creation of apprehension in the mind of the accused that he would not get fair justice from the Divisional Special Judge, Barisal and such grounds do not appear to us bonafide. Therefore, on those grounds the case could not be transferred. It further appears that the High Court Division without issuing any Rule upon the State disposed of the application transferring the case from the Divisional Special Judge to the Sessions Judge, Barisal. We do not approve this kind of exercise of power by the High Court Division. The High Court Division committed prima-facie error in passing the impugned Order, but since examination of the prosecution has already been completed and now the case is at the stage of examination of defence witnesses, we are not inclined to grant leave as that would delay the disposal of the case, instead we are inclined to dispose of the leave petition setting aside the Order passed by the High Court Division. 

 The impugned Order dated 18-7-20 10 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 20319 of 2010 summarily disposing of the application filed by the accused-respondent under section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure transferring Special Case No. 7 of 2009 from the Court of Divisional Special Judge, Barisal to the Sessions Judge, Barisal is set aside. The Divisional Special Judge, Barisal is directed to dispose of the case as expeditiously as possible.
